12. Explain the following rules. a) Maxwell’s right-hand thumb rule to show the direction of the management field produced when an electric current flows through a straight wire. Ans:- If a straight conductor is held in the right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of electric current, then the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field lines produced around the conductor. b) Maxwell’s right-hand grip rule to find the direction of magnetic field lines of force around a solenoid. Ans:- If a solenoid is gripped with the right hand so that the fingers curl in the direction of current through the turns, then the extended thumb points in the direction of the magnetic field inside the solenoid, indicating its north pole. 13. How can the magnetic field around straight current carrying wire be demonstrated by using iron dust, cardboard, and conducting straight wire? Explain it. Ans:- The magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire can be demonstrated by passing the wire vertically through a small hole at the center of a cardboard sheet. The cardboard is placed horizontally, and fine iron dust (iron filings) is sprinkled uniformly on it. When the wire is connected to a battery and current flows through it, the iron dust rearranges itself in concentric circular patterns around the wire. This shows that a magnetic field is produced around the current-carrying conductor. The direction of the magnetic field can be understood using the right-hand thumb rule, and the closeness of the circles near the wire indicates that the magnetic field is stronger closer to the conductor.

14. Study the given picture and wire what happens in following situations. i) As the bar magnet is slowly introduced into the solenoid. Ans:- When the bar magnet is slowly introduced into the solenoid, The galvanometer shows a small deflection, indicating that a weak induced current is produced due to the slow change in magnetic flux. ii) While introducing the bar magnet rapidly into the solenoid. Ans:- When the bar magnet is introduced rapidly into the solenoid, The galvanometer shows a large deflection, indicating that a stronger induced current is produced due to the rapid change in magnetic flux. iii) Holding the bar magnet stationary inside the solenoid. Ans:- When the bar magnet is held stationary inside the solenoid, The galvanometer shows no deflection because there is no change in magnetic flux and hence no induced current is produced. iv) On pulling the bar magnet quickly out of the solenoid. Ans:- When the bar magnet is pulled quickly out of the solenoid, The galvanometer shows a large deflection in the opposite direction, indicating that a strong induced current is produced in the reverse direction due to the rapid decrease in magnetic flux.

Uses of Step-up Transformer are given below, 1. It is used at power stations to increase voltage for long-distance transmission of electric power, reducing energy loss. 2. It is used in devices like X-ray machines and microwave ovens where high voltage is required.

Uses of Step-down Transformer are given below, 1. It is used in substations to reduce high transmission voltage to a safe level for domestic and industrial use. 2. It is used in adapters and chargers (mobile chargers, laptop chargers) to obtain low voltage from the mains supply. ***
